newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OPEC AGREES TO OIL OUTPUT FREEZE - LUKMAN.
newsitem.headline: OPEC AGREES TO OIL OUTPUT FREEZE - LUKMAN.

text.p: OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman said on Wednesday that the producer group had agreed to a freeze of its 25.033 million barrels per day (bpd) ceiling.
Asked by reporters at the end of a closed session if the group had agreed to freeze its ceiling, Lukman said: "Yes".
Lukman said the freeze on the ceiling would be for six months, up to the end of this year.

He also said that the group's members had agreed to go back to their production allocations and added that "no threats" had been made to overproducers. He confirmed all individual quotas have been left unchanged.
Lukman said that ministers expected the meeting to be wrapped up on Thursday when they meet again at 0800 GMT.

OPEC President Abdullah Salem al-Badri, the Libyan oil minister, told reporters: "we had a frank discussion and one by one everyone agreed to adhere to quota over the next six months, and now the markets will judge".
